<div class="container">
    <div class="guide-header">
        <div class="breadcrumb"><a href="/">Home</a> / <a href="/guides/">Guides</a> / DevSecOps</div>
        <h1>DevSecOps Pipeline Security</h1>
        <span class="new-badge"><i class="fas fa-infinity"></i> DevOps</span>
        <p style="color: var(--text-muted); font-size: 1.1rem; margin-top: 1rem;">Integrate security into CI/CD
            pipelines with SAST, DAST, SCA, and shift-left practices.</p>
        <div class="meta" style="margin-top: 1rem;">
            <div class="meta-item"><i class="fas fa-book-open"></i> 20 min read</div>
            <div class="meta-item"><i class="fas fa-crosshairs"></i> Intermediate</div>
            <div class="meta-item"><i class="far fa-calendar-alt"></i> Jan 17, 2026</div>
        </div>
    </div>

    <article class="content">
        <img src="/images/guides/devsecops-pipeline-security.png" alt="DevSecOps Pipeline Security Guide"
            class="featured-image" loading="lazy">

        <p>Traditional security testing at the end of development is too slow and too expensive. DevSecOps shifts
            security left - integrating automated security testing throughout the CI/CD pipeline so vulnerabilities
            are found when they're cheapest to fix.</p>

        <div class="info-box">
            <strong><i class="fas fa-lightbulb"></i> Why Shift-Left Security?</strong>
            <p style="margin-top: 0.5rem; margin-bottom: 0;">A vulnerability found in development costs
                <strong>$80</strong> to fix. Found in testing: <strong>$240</strong>. Found in production:
                <strong>$7,600</strong>. The earlier you find it, the cheaper it is. (Source: IBM Systems Sciences
                Institute)</p>
        </div>

        <div class="toc">
            <h3><i class="fas fa-list-ul"></i> Table of Contents</h3>
            <ul>
                <li><a href="#overview">1. DevSecOps Overview</a></li>
                <li><a href="#sast">2. SAST - Static Application Security Testing</a></li>
                <li><a href="#sca">3. SCA - Software Composition Analysis</a></li>
                <li><a href="#secrets">4. Secrets Detection</a></li>
                <li><a href="#dast">5. DAST - Dynamic Application Security Testing</a></li>
                <li><a href="#container">6. Container Security</a></li>
                <li><a href="#iac">7. Infrastructure as Code Security</a></li>
                <li><a href="#pipeline">8. Complete Pipeline Example</a></li>
            </ul>
        </div>

        <h2 id="overview">1. DevSecOps Overview</h2>

        <h3>The DevSecOps Pipeline</h3>
        <p>Security checks at every stage:</p>

        <table>
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Stage</th>
                    <th>Security Activity</th>
                    <th>Tools</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
                <tr>
                    <td><strong>Code</strong></td>
                    <td>Pre-commit hooks, secrets scanning</td>
                    <td>GitLeaks, pre-commit</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td><strong>Build</strong></td>
                    <td>SAST, SCA, license compliance</td>
                    <td>Semgrep, Snyk, FOSSA</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td><strong>Test</strong></td>
                    <td>DAST, API security testing</td>
                    <td>OWASP ZAP, Nuclei</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td><strong>Deploy</strong></td>
                    <td>Container scanning, IaC scanning</td>
                    <td>Trivy, Checkov</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td><strong>Production</strong></td>
                    <td>RASP, WAF, monitoring</td>
                    <td>Datadog, Falco</td>
                </tr>
            </tbody>
        </table>

        <h2 id="sast">2. SAST - Static Application Security Testing</h2>

        <p>SAST analyzes source code to find vulnerabilities without running the application.</p>

        <h3>Popular SAST Tools</h3>
        <table>
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Tool</th>
                    <th>Languages</th>
                    <th>Highlights</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
                <tr>
                    <td><strong>Semgrep</strong></td>
                    <td>30+ languages</td>
                    <td>Fast, open-source, custom rules</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td><strong>SonarQube</strong></td>
                    <td>25+ languages</td>
                    <td>Quality + security, self-hosted</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td><strong>CodeQL</strong></td>
                    <td>10+ languages</td>
                    <td>GitHub native, query-based</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td><strong>Checkmarx</strong></td>
                    <td>25+ languages</td>
                    <td>Enterprise, accurate</td>
                </tr>
            </tbody>
        </table>

        <h3>GitHub Actions: Semgrep Example</h3>

        <div class="pipeline-box">
            <h5><i class="fas fa-code-branch"></i> .github/workflows/sast.yml</h5>
            <pre><code><span class="yaml-key">name:</span> <span class="yaml-value">SAST Scan</span>

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs: semgrep: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4

  - <span class="yaml-key">name:</span> <span class="yaml-value">Run Semgrep</span>
    <span class="yaml-key">uses:</span> <span class="yaml-value">returntocorp/semgrep-action@v1</span>
    <span class="yaml-key">with:</span>
      <span class="yaml-key">config:</span> <span class="yaml-value">p/security-audit p/owasp-top-ten</span>
    <span class="yaml-key">env:</span>
      <span class="yaml-key">SEMGREP_APP_TOKEN:</span> <span class="yaml-value">${{ secrets.SEMGREP_APP_TOKEN }}</span></code></pre>
        </div>

        <h2 id="sca">3. SCA - Software Composition Analysis</h2>

        <p>SCA scans dependencies for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) and license issues.</p>

        <div class="warning-box">
            <strong><i class="fas fa-exclamation-triangle"></i> Supply Chain Risk</strong>
            <p style="margin-top: 0.5rem; margin-bottom: 0;">Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) showed how a single
                vulnerable dependency can affect thousands of applications. SCA is critical for modern software.</p>
        </div>

        <h3>Popular SCA Tools</h3>
        <table>
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Tool</th>
                    <th>Ecosystems</th>
                    <th>Highlights</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
                <tr>
                    <td><strong>Snyk</strong></td>
                    <td>npm, Maven, pip, Go, etc.</td>
                    <td>Fix PRs, container scanning</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td><strong>Dependabot</strong></td>
                    <td>GitHub native</td>
                    <td>Free, auto PR updates</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td><strong>OWASP Dependency-Check</strong></td>
                    <td>Java, .NET, npm, etc.</td>
                    <td>Open-source, offline</td>
                </tr>
                <tr>
                    <td><strong>Renovate</strong></td>
                    <td>All major</td>
                    <td>Highly configurable</td>
                </tr>
            </tbody>
        </table>

        <h3>GitHub Actions: Snyk Example</h3>

        <div class="pipeline-box">
            <h5><i class="fas fa-shield-alt"></i> SCA with Snyk</h5>
            <pre><code><span class="yaml-key">- name:</span> <span class="yaml-value">Run Snyk</span>

uses: snyk/actions/node@master env: SNYK_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SNYK_TOKEN }} with: args: –severity-threshold=high 

        <h2 id="secrets">4. Secrets Detection</h2>

        <p>Prevent API keys, passwords, and tokens from reaching your repository.</p>

        <h3>Pre-Commit Secrets Scanning</h3>

        <div class="pipeline-box">
            <h5><i class="fas fa-key"></i> .pre-commit-config.yaml</h5>
            <pre><code><span class="yaml-key">repos:</span>

  • repo: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks rev: v8.18.0 hooks:

    • id: gitleaks

  • repo: https://github.com/Yelp/detect-secrets rev: v1.4.0 hooks:

    • id: detect-secrets args: [‘–baseline’, ‘.secrets.baseline’] 

      <h3>CI Pipeline Secrets Scanning</h3>
<pre><code><span class="yaml-comment"># GitLeaks in GitHub Actions</span>

- name: GitLeaks Scan uses: gitleaks/gitleaks-action@v2 env: GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

        <h2 id="dast">5. DAST - Dynamic Application Security Testing</h2>

        <p>DAST tests running applications by simulating real attacks.</p>

        <h3>OWASP ZAP in CI/CD</h3>

        <div class="pipeline-box">
            <h5><i class="fas fa-spider"></i> DAST with OWASP ZAP</h5>
            <pre><code><span class="yaml-key">- name:</span> <span class="yaml-value">ZAP Baseline Scan</span>

uses: zaproxy/action-baseline@v0.10.0 with: target: ‘https://staging.myapp.com’ rules_file_name: ‘.zap/rules.tsv’ issue_title: ‘ZAP Security Scan Results’ 

        <h3>When to Use DAST</h3>
        <ul>
            <li><strong>Staging environment</strong> - After deployment to staging</li>
            <li><strong>Nightly builds</strong> - Full scan on main branch</li>
            <li><strong>Pre-release</strong> - Before production deployment</li>
        </ul>

        <h2 id="container">6. Container Security</h2>

        <p>Scan container images for vulnerabilities before deployment.</p>

        <h3>Trivy Container Scanning</h3>

        <div class="pipeline-box">
            <h5><i class="fas fa-docker"></i> Container Scan with Trivy</h5>
            <pre><code><span class="yaml-key">- name:</span> <span class="yaml-value">Build Image</span>

run: docker build -t myapp:${{ github.sha }} .

- name: Trivy Scan uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master with: image-ref: ‘myapp:${{ github.sha }}’ format: ‘sarif’ exit-code: ‘1’ severity: ‘CRITICAL,HIGH’ 

        <h2 id="iac">7. Infrastructure as Code Security</h2>

        <p>Scan Terraform, CloudFormation, and Kubernetes manifests for misconfigurations.</p>

        <h3>Checkov IaC Scanning</h3>

        <div class="pipeline-box">
            <h5><i class="fas fa-cloud"></i> IaC Security with Checkov</h5>
            <pre><code><span class="yaml-key">- name:</span> <span class="yaml-value">Checkov Scan</span>

uses: bridgecrewio/checkov-action@master with: directory: terraform/ framework: terraform soft_fail: false skip_check: CKV_AWS_18,CKV_AWS_21 

        <h2 id="pipeline">8. Complete Pipeline Example</h2>

        <div class="success-box">
            <strong><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> Full DevSecOps Pipeline</strong>
            <p style="margin-top: 0.5rem; margin-bottom: 0;">This example combines all security tools into a
                comprehensive CI/CD workflow.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="pipeline-box">
            <h5><i class="fas fa-infinity"></i> Complete .github/workflows/devsecops.yml</h5>
            <pre><code><span class="yaml-key">name:</span> <span class="yaml-value">DevSecOps Pipeline</span>

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs: secrets-scan: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: fetch-depth: 0 - uses: gitleaks/gitleaks-action@v2

sast: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: returntocorp/semgrep-action@v1 with: config: p/security-audit

sca: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: snyk/actions/node@master env: SNYK_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SNYK_TOKEN }}

container-scan: needs: [sast, sca] runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - run: docker build -t app:${{ github.sha }} . - uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master with: image-ref: ‘app:${{ github.sha }}’ exit-code: ‘1’ severity: ‘CRITICAL,HIGH’

dast: needs: [container-scan] if: github.ref == ‘refs/heads/main’ runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: zaproxy/action-baseline@v0.10.0 with: target: ‘https://staging.example.com’ 

        <div class="info-box">
            <strong><i class="fas fa-lightbulb"></i> Key Takeaways</strong>
            <ul style="margin-top: 0.5rem; margin-bottom: 0;">
                <li>Start with secrets scanning and SAST - they're fast and catch common issues</li>
                <li>Add SCA next - dependency vulnerabilities are a major risk</li>
                <li>Container scanning before any deployment</li>
                <li>DAST on staging/pre-prod - not every commit (too slow)</li>
                <li>Don't fail builds on every finding - prioritize critical/high first</li>
            </ul>
        </div>

        <p
            style="margin-top: 3rem; padding-top: 2rem; border-top: 1px solid var(--border); color: var(--text-muted);">

        </p>

                <a href="#" onclick="shareLinkedIn(event)" class="share-btn"><i class="fab fa-linkedin-in"></i></a>
                <button onclick="copyLink()" class="share-btn"><i class="fas fa-link"></i></button>
            </div>
            <div class="button-separator"></div>
            <button onclick="printArticle()" class="print-btn"><i class="fas fa-print"></i></button>
        </div>
    </div>

</div>
